The morphological call was not fabricated: high-dose wells showed extreme actin texture and heterogeneity (act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0 at 10 uM, +19.4 at 3 uM, act_std z=+16.3) with dose-monotonic rho=+1.00, reduced solidity and lower density visually described as stellate retraction, and nearest-atlas matches enriched for actin disruptors. That evidence correctly captured a strong cytoskeletal remodeling phenotype.

The error was equating phenocopy with direct target. Unblinded bryostatin binds protein kinase C (PMID 2001329) and activates downstream kinase signaling (PMID 18765827), while PKC signaling directly modulates actin cytoskeleton organization (PMID 10526317) via regulators such as MARCKS actin crosslinking (PMID 1560845). A kinase modulator can therefore produce a near-perfect actin-disruptor texture signature without binding actin.

I was misled by the magnitude and monotonicity of act_glcm_contrast/act_std/tub_glcm_contrast and by confirmatory describe_phenotype and compare_to_reference_atlas outputs, and my acquisition choices focused only on the strong high-dose range (0.3, 1, 3, 10 uM) with no low-dose onset, no kinase-reference comparison, and no phospho-signaling or washout/polymerization readout to discriminate direct depolymerization from upstream kinase-mediated remodeling.

what_was_wrong: Concluded direct actin disruption instead of kinase-inhibitor mechanism; missed PKC-mediated downstream actin remodeling by bryostatin.

Acquisition strategy sampled only emergent-to-maximal doses (0.3 to 10 uM) to confirm actin trend, with no low-dose, replicate, reversibility, or biochemical polymerization test to challenge direct actin binding.

## Unblinding

Compound: **bryostatin** (PubChem CID [6435419](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6435419))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Actin disruptors**, BBBC021 annotates **Kinase inhibitors**.

## Reflection

The morphological call was not fabricated: high-dose wells showed extreme actin texture and heterogeneity (act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0 at 10 uM, +19.4 at 3 uM, act_std z=+16.3) with dose-monotonic rho=+1.00, reduced solidity and lower density visually described as stellate retraction, and nearest-atlas matches enriched for actin disruptors. That evidence correctly captured a strong cytoskeletal remodeling phenotype.

The error was equating phenocopy with direct target. Unblinded bryostatin binds protein kinase C (PMID 2001329) and activates downstream kinase signaling (PMID 18765827), while PKC signaling directly modulates actin cytoskeleton organization (PMID 10526317) via regulators such as MARCKS actin crosslinking (PMID 1560845). A kinase modulator can therefore produce a near-perfect actin-disruptor texture signature without binding actin.

I was misled by the magnitude and monotonicity of act_glcm_contrast/act_std/tub_glcm_contrast and by confirmatory describe_phenotype and compare_to_reference_atlas outputs, and my acquisition choices focused only on the strong high-dose range (0.3, 1, 3, 10 uM) with no low-dose onset, no kinase-reference comparison, and no phospho-signaling or washout/polymerization readout to discriminate direct depolymerization from upstream kinase-mediated remodeling.

What was right:
- High-dose actin texture/heterogeneity signal was real and dose-monotonic: act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0 at 10 uM and +19.4 at 3 uM with Spearman rho=+1.00 for act_glcm_contrast, act_std and tub_glcm_contrast.
- Visual and shape features correctly reported cytoskeletal remodeling: lower density vs DMSO, cell_solidity z=-15.9 at 3 uM and nuc_eccentricity shifts at 0.3-1 uM.
- Atlas similarity to actin disruptors (3/10) reflected genuine morphological phenocopy, not instrument error.

What was wrong or missed:
- Concluded direct actin disruption instead of kinase-inhibitor mechanism; missed PKC-mediated downstream actin remodeling by bryostatin.
- Overweighted e2/e11 actin z-scores, e5 microscopist actin call, and e6 atlas actin enrichment without testing kinase-inhibitor alternatives or phospho-PKC/MARCKS readouts.
- Acquisition strategy sampled only emergent-to-maximal doses (0.3 to 10 uM) to confirm actin trend, with no low-dose, replicate, reversibility, or biochemical polymerization test to challenge direct actin binding.

Proposed next experiment: Compare bryostatin to direct actin controls (cytochalasin D) and PKC controls in parallel: phospho-PKC substrate / phospho-MARCKS immunofluorescence with PKC-inhibitor rescue plus a cell-free actin polymerization assay to test for direct depolymerization versus signaling-mediated remodeling.
